title: Orbit: embeddable runbook bundle scheduler for quick admin utilities
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary: Build 'Orbit', a lightweight scheduler and packaging layer that turns curated runbook fragments (patchlets) into embeddable admin workflows. Orbit allows support tools (console buttons, CLI quickflows, and internal chat ops) to attach a small, versioned runbook bundle to a request and ask the scheduler to execute it as a single idempotent transaction with full audit and telemetry.

Why this exists: Current runbooks are long-form and not easily composable into short, repeatable admin utilities. Support agents and first-line responders need fast, safe, reproducible actions (e.g., rotate-api-key, hotfix-config, cache-evict) with clear rollback and telemetry. Orbit is intended to reduce mean time to remediate (MTTR) for common operational incidents while preserving safety and observability.

Core ideas/constraints:
- Patchlets: small, typed runbook fragments with inputs, outputs, and pre/post checks.
- Bundle scheduler: receives a bundle manifest, schedules execution in an isolated worker, enforces idempotency token and run-time limits, manages backoff and retries.
- Safety sandbox: dry-run mode and a staged canary that runs first against a shadow environment, then production with RBAC gating.
- Telemetry bridge: emit structured audit events (actor, bundle_sha, tokens_used, pre-checks, outcomes) to the Console telemetry pipeline and to the incident dashboard.
- Observability targets: end-to-end median execution latency < 2s for quick patchlets; 99th percentile < 10s for composite bundles (goal depends on patchlet IO).
- Compatibility: bundles must be addressable from Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments (Orbit control plane only stores metadata; execution can be routed to appropriate runtime per customer policy).

Non-goals: not a full workflow engine for complex, long-running orchestrations; does not replace existing orchestrator for multi-step, multi-team incidents.

Integration points and artifacts:
- Design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/OPS/Orbit+Runbook+Embedding (draft)
- API proto (internal): https://github.com/redwood-inference/orbit/pull/112 (WIP)
- Console mockups: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/orbit-console-mockups
- Incident dashboard prototype: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/ops/orbit-exec-traces

Telemetry & security: Orbit will log audit records to the centralized audit log (KMS-encrypted) and attach immutable run descriptors. All executions require an RBAC check; requests originating from the Console will carry token introspection. For private deployments the control plane will store pointers only; execution happens in-customer where required.
acceptance_criteria: Can accept a bundle manifest (JSON) and return an execution id synchronously
Execution id resolves to an audit record with actor, bundle_sha, inputs, and final status
Dry-run mode executes pre-checks without mutating state and returns deterministic findings
Idempotency: re-sending the same idempotency token within 24 hours returns same terminal status
RBAC gating works: users without run permission receive 403 and no execution occurs
Telemetry: events appear in the Orbit Grafana dashboard and Console timeline within 30s
